value.declaration: Choose a common H^gamma bound A=A(T,gamma,R) for source data in the indicated ball, using E001's a priori bound and the explicit Sobolev norm comparison.
For the datum under L3, choose its unique smooth exact solution from N001.
Construct V by Interp from the smooth twisted Scheme trajectory, whose continuity is supplied by N007.

patches.value: H001-H003 fix T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. By N001 choose the common exact-solution bound M=1+A(T,gamma,R); it is independent of the datum in the ball. Let K0>=1 dominate the constant in N010 for this M. Fix arbitrary smooth q and integer L, and assume L3: q is real and mean-zero with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R, and L>0. Then N007 gives a global smooth finite-step trajectory and continuous interpolation. N001 gives the smooth exact solution, so e=v-V is continuous, starts at zero, and exists on the full interval. The constants M,K0 are chosen before q and L and involve no higher Sobolev norm. In what follows the only temporary restriction on error size is the bootstrap used to invoke N010.

Set tau0=min(1,delta/2,(1/(4*K))^(1/gamma))>0. If L2: the error first reached norm one at some time t*, continuity and e(0)=0 give an error supremum <=1 on [0,t*]. F003, including its partial-last-block case, then gives ||e(t*)||_2<=K*tau^gamma<=1/4, a contradiction. Discharge L2; continuity excludes all crossings and yields sup_[0,T]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma. At grid points N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)U^n and N006 gives unitarity, so the grid error equals ||u(t_n)-U^n||_2. Rename K as C, quantify the smooth datum and all L with tau<=tau0, and retain the constants chosen before them. Discharge L3; this proves the smooth-data estimate, uniformly in spectral support and higher norms.
